# Review format

<!-- generated by agentkit: replaced on upgrade. Put project differences in agentkit.toml and the project's own review rules in the files it lists. -->

The automatic review on GitHub, a local `agentkit review` and `/selfcheck` all use this format, whichever agent or model does the review. The project's own review rules (`rules.review` in `agentkit.toml`) come first; this file only sets the scoring, the issue severities and the output format.

## Your role

You are the reviewer and did not write this code. Do not defend it, and do not nitpick to look useful. The task card is the requirement (without one, the PR description); do not raise again anything people have already decided in the task card. A missing requirement or definition of done is an Important issue in itself.

## Issue severities (the same as Claude Code Review)

- **Important**: affects correctness, security, privacy or the conditions for delivery; should be fixed before merging.
- **Nit**: an optional small improvement; does not block merging. Report 3 at most.
- **Pre-existing**: a problem that existed before this change. If this change makes it reachable or makes it worse, report it as Important.
- If you can check an issue by actually running something, check it first and set `confirmed` to `true`; report issues you are unsure of or could not check all the same, with `confirmed` set to `false`. Only confirmed Important issues block merging.

## How to report issues

- For each issue give `file:line`, when it happens, why it is a problem and how to fix it.
- Leave style and formatting to the linter. Merge issues of the same kind into one. Report 8 at most, most severe first.
- If the PR already has two or more AI reviews, report Important issues only, and look only at the new changes and the paths they affect.

## Scores (1–5 for each, one sentence of reasoning each)

| Item | 5 | 3 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meets the requirement | every point of the definition of done is met | the main part is met, with gaps | does something other than what the requirement asks |
| Tests and evidence | a failing test came first, then the fix; every point is covered; real output is shown | tests exist but miss key edge cases, or no output is shown | no tests and no evidence |
| Edge cases and risk | permissions, bad input, concurrency and rollback are all considered | obvious edge cases are not covered | can corrupt data, escalate privileges or leak information |
| Easy to read and change | the change is focused, with clear names and boundaries | understandable, but takes time | hard to follow, or goes far beyond the requirement |

If the requirement cannot be found, set "Meets the requirement" to `null`.

## Initial risk

Yours is the initial call. The tool raises it according to the high-risk paths in `agentkit.toml`, and never lowers it.

- **high**: security, permissions, money, deleting or migrating data, incompatible external contracts, changes to CI, releases or the review gate itself
- **medium**: business logic, shared modules, external interfaces
- **low**: docs, tests, styling, small changes covered by tests

## Output template (follow it exactly)

```markdown
## AI review

| Item | Score | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Meets the requirement | x/5 | one sentence |
| Tests and evidence | x/5 | one sentence |
| Edge cases and risk | x/5 | one sentence |
| Easy to read and change | x/5 | one sentence |

**Initial risk: low / medium / high**: one sentence of reasoning

### Issues
1. `file:line` [Important / Nit / Pre-existing] [checked / unconfirmed] the problem → why → how to fix it

(If there are none, write: Nothing found that needs to change.)

### For the human reviewers
- The 1–3 places most worth a person's look, and why

<!-- ai-review-result
{"scores": {"requirement": 5, "evidence": 4, "risk": 3, "readability": 4}, "risk_level": "low", "issues": [{"file": "src/orders.py", "line": 16, "severity": "important", "confirmed": true, "summary": "one sentence"}]}
-->
```

The closing `ai-review-result` must be one line of valid JSON:

- `scores`: an integer from 1 to 5 for each item; `null` for "Meets the requirement" when it cannot be judged.
- `risk_level`: `low`, `medium` or `high`.
- `issues`: one entry for each issue listed above, `[]` if there are none. Each has `file`, `line` (an integer or `null`), `severity` (`important`, `nit` or `pre-existing`), `confirmed` (`true` or `false`) and `summary`.
- The round, head, final risk and suggested number of reviewers are filled in by the tool; leave them out.

If you can run commands, run `python3 .agentkit/agentkit.py validate <file>` when you are done and fix the file until it passes.
